Definition: from G4862 and the base of G1553; a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller:--companion in travel, travel with.
BiblicalUsage: The brother chosen by the churches to travel with Paul on the work of grace, and Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul's companions in travel, seized in the riot at Ephesus, share the road with him. A fellow traveller is not a tourist but a companion in the work, chosen by the churches and caught by the same mob.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the gospel travels in company, and I believe a companion on the road is a gift of the churches and of God.
